title: Your Copilot Has No Memory — Why RAG Fails and LLM Wiki Fixes It
description:
Copilot can answer a question perfectly today and fumble the same question tomorrow because it searches instead of remembering. This episode explains why RAG-based Copilot stays shallow and how the LLM Wiki pattern adds compiled, maintained knowledge, for IT leaders and Microsoft 365 architects. You learn how a hybrid Copilot with a wiki layer improves consistency, trust and governance.
In this episode
00:00 – Copilot searches, it doesn't remember03:37 – What RAG actually does05:59 – The stateless trap10:55 – Enter the LLM Wiki16:00 – Where Copilot's retrieval lives26:36 – Trust and redundant knowledge40:33 – Scale and hybrid Copilot45:42 – Governance and getting started
Key takeaways
Copilot's Graph grounding is retrieval-augmented generation, which searches from zero on every query and therefore cannot build memory or consistency over time.The LLM Wiki pattern compiles raw sources once into maintained, cross-linked pages governed by a schema and flags contradictions instead of silently averaging them.Start with one recurring high-value knowledge domain, clean up its sources with retention, content types and ownership, and give a named owner responsibility for the schema.
Worth quoting
“Retrieval and memory are not the same thing. One finds information, the other builds on what it already knows.” – Mirko Peters (00:23)
“You can't prompt your way out of an architecture that has no place to store what it learns.” – Mirko Peters (09:54)
